segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
49. And here the Jews were freed from tribute.
And in that same year the second history of the Maccabees ended.
And in the eighth year of Ptolemy, son of Habuba {Euergetes II / Physcon?}, Demetrius died {OCR?: ܒܛܠ or ܡܝܬ? / ܒܛܓ reads like error for a verb of dying/ceasing};
and in his place Antiochus Sidetes reigned over Syria,
and he came against Jerusalem to wage war.
And certain slaves rebelled in Sicily,
and when they were besieged in one of the cities of the island,
they ate one another out of hunger.
And on the island of Aeolus a great eruption of fire took place.
And the general of Ptolemy, the one in Jericho,
in the fifteenth year of the same Ptolemy,
killed Simon the high priest.
And John arose after him,
who was called Hyrcanus,
because he gathered an army against the king of Hyrcania and went to war [for / he ruled for] twenty-six years.
And in the seventeenth year of this Ptolemy,
Demetrius returned again to the kingdom,
and he reigned over Syria another four years.
And Antiochus Grypus arose after him over Syria for twelve {OCR: ܐܢܝܐ for ܫܢܝܐ} years.
And he came against Jerusalem,
and besieged it severely.
Then Hyrcanus, being hard pressed,
opened the tomb of David and took out of it three thousand talents of gold, which had been hidden there by the ancients,
and gave three hundred talents of them to Antiochus,
and he departed from him.
And at this time Hyrcanus {OCR: ܘܝܪܩܢܘܣ for ܗܝܪܩܢܘܣ} devastated Samaria.
[Ptolemy] after Soter, who is also called Physcon (Physcon,
Physkon), [ruled for] seventeen years.
In his fourth year Antiochus Cyzicenus {OCR?: ܩܘܙܝܩܘܣ} reigned in Syria for eighteen years.
And in the eleventh year of Soter, John Hyrcanus died,
and Aristobulus son of Jonathan {John} arose for one year.
This man put on a crown.
And his brother Antigonus was killed by treachery {or: he killed his brother Antigonus by treachery}.
And another brother of his, John, killed this man in turn,
who is Ioannes,
and he was also called Alexander.
And he reigned for twenty-seven years.
This man ruled the people harshly.
And in his time Ptolemy Soter was driven out by Cleopatra his mother,
and he fled to the island of Cyprus.
